ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD drawn as a rhombus, with vertices labeled A at the upper left, B at the upper right, C at the lower right, and D at the lower left. Both diagonals AC and BD are drawn, and they intersect at point E inside the rhombus. Reasoning: The given angle m∠ABD = 55° is the angle between side BA and diagonal BD at vertex B. In a rhombus, a diagonal bisects the angles at its endpoints, so diagonal BD bisects ∠ABC. Therefore m∠ABC = 2 × 55° = 110°. Since a rhombus is a parallelogram, adjacent interior angles are supplementary, so m∠BCD = 180° − 110° = 70°. Diagonal AC bisects the angle at C in a rhombus, so m∠ACB = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as quadrilateral ABCD with side AB adjacent to AD and BC, and diagonal AC drawn from A to C. From the text, ABCD is a rhombus, so all sides are equal; in particular AB = AD and AB = BC. Since m∠ABD = 55° and triangle ABD has AB = AD, triangle ABD is isosceles, so ∠ADB = 55° as well. Hence ∠BAD = 180° - 55° - 55° = 70°. Because a rhombus is a parallelogram, adjacent angles are supplementary, so ∠ABC = 180° - 70° = 110°. Now consider triangle ABC in the diagram: AB = BC, so triangle ABC is isosceles with base AC, making ∠BAC = ∠ACB. Therefore ∠ACB = (180° - 110°)/2 = 35°.
